analysis:
Both units are head-only excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, lines 231-595. No patch or base text was supplied, so I could not tell which entries this PR added. I made no source or code-level assessment, and no line is cited as evidence of a regression. These notes are descriptions for later passes, not confirmed security findings.

Described behaviors relevant to existing threats:
- Frozen legacy MDM cohort and /v1/enroll proof (lines 249-258): this matches the TB-009 and TB-011 limitations already in the canonical model. The changelog restates that generic profiles stay copyable.
- Base rewards (line 252): they require macOS 27+ and qualified App Attest (T-052, T-055).
- Transient provider-token store failures (line 257): they now return 1013 on WebSocket registration and 503 on enrollment. This touches T-006 and T-039 availability behavior, and unauthorized handling for invalid credentials is unchanged.
- Attestation challenges (line 523) and App Attest protocol 3 only (line 525): both fail closed (T-036, T-052).
- T-031 (line 521): the wallet earnings endpoint is removed.
- SSD cache changes (lines 545-553, 235-238, 462-464): the SSD cache TTL moves from 15 to 30 minutes, with a SEC-035 re-acceptance claimed. The write budget rises to 750 GB/day, and capture and write gating changes. These matter to T-041 and T-016.
- Cache-routing persistence (lines 423-427): it stores holders and demand in the database, with no prompts or raw chain hashes persisted. A later pass should check whether T-041 and T-058 need updates.
- Other entries: the OpenRouter-based PR review workflow (lines 459-461, 280-286), cache pricing and billing (lines 496-504), and model artifact revisions (lines 466-480) all touch billing or supply-chain surfaces.

Coverage limit: no source code was provided, so none of these claims are verified.
